title:
A stock-research
harness
notes: Three hours, including two ten-minute breaks. This lecture builds on the portfolio and stock-analysis work in Lectures 2 and 4. The emphasis is the reasoning behind tool, memory, and recovery policies. Slides 1–51 form the live route. Slides 52–57 are reference material. Keep lesson.md available for the fuller explanations and exercises.
subtitle:
Special Topics
Pydantic AI Harness
Yang Guo · November 5, 2026

title: The research question
body: How concentrated is our portfolio, and how do the stocks compare on historical risk?
What evidence should the harness collect, remember, and cite before it accepts an answer?
notes: Spend the opening on what would count as a useful answer. Students should name holdings, cash, prices, dates, risk conventions, and sources. Add the operational requirement: the research may span several runs. Ask how we would know which work is complete after closing the terminal. The application will need both evidence and task state. Introduce the final report now so each component has a visible purpose.

title: The analysis we already know
table: Lots, weighted cost, issuer exposure, cash
callout: Prices 100, 110, 99 give a total return of −1%.
notes: Spend no more than five minutes reviewing calculations. Run the opening of 01_data_and_tools.py. The weighted entry price for the AAPL lots is 95, not the unweighted mean 97.5. Raw close values the actual shares. Adjusted prices drive return calculations. Cash belongs in the portfolio denominator. Sources: ../Lecture 2/3_pandas_to_portfolio.ipynb, ../Lecture 4/3_stock_analysis_template.ipynb, ../Lecture 4/4_running_analysis_at_scale.ipynb. These calculations remain ordinary Python functions.

title: One turn of the agent loop
table: Validate arguments, run Python, return result
Include the observation in the next request
notes: A tool call contains a name, arguments, and a call ID. The runtime connects the result to that ID. The model chooses an action but Python executes it. Ask whether saving a file automatically changes the next model request. It does not: a context or retrieval policy must load it. Persistent memory affects future model inputs rather than trained parameters. Run 02_agent_and_tools.py for the smallest example. Its FunctionModel controls the choices while the real Pydantic runtime executes the loop. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools/.

title: Responsibility boundaries
table: Ticker queue and accepted task state
Restart policy and stable evidence IDs
notes: Open the capability list in research_harness/agent.py. Then identify runner.py, tools.py, and report.py. A plan marked complete is a statement by the model. The application accepts the ticker only after validating and saving a research note. This distinction will recur when we discuss checkpoints and longer projects. The lecture pins pydantic-ai-harness 0.65.0 and pydantic-ai-slim 2.65.0 in uv.lock. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/.

title: The tool contract
table: Whole records, citation IDs, omission count
Returned evidence and a retrieval event
notes: Ask students to define the contract before showing the function signature. The model needs freedom to choose useful search terms. The project already determines which ticker and date apply. Explain that a tool contract also includes preconditions, side effects, and retry behavior. The dispatcher rechecks the input hashes and active task. An identical returned record reuses its evidence ID. A successful search alone does not complete research.

title: Model arguments and dependencies
notes: This is an excerpt of the registered research tool. Open the full function to follow the dispatch call. RunContext does not become a model-supplied argument. The function signature and annotations define the query schema. Python injects ResearchDeps. Ask what could go wrong if the model supplied an unrestricted project path or namespace. The application should own those boundaries. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/dependencies/.

title: Choosing tool granularity
table: Broad flexibility needs explicit access controls
More model requests and partial results
A research choice the model can usefully make
notes: Do not present one granularity as universally correct. A SQL tool can work with a restricted database role, bound parameters where applicable, query limits, and clear scope. Tiny arithmetic tools can be helpful in some workflows but are wasteful when the calculation is already defined. Our risk function produces a complete, reproducible observation. Source search remains a model decision because the next useful query depends on the evidence already found. Ask students where a leverage-ratio tool would fit.

title: Four validation boundaries
table: Are required fields, types, and ranges valid?
Is the request meaningful for this project?
Are values, dates, units, and IDs intact?
Does the final note meet the research contract?
notes: Explain coercion: Pydantic can convert some values unless strict validation is configured. Passing the schema therefore means satisfying this schema, not establishing permission or sufficient data. A valid integer window can still exceed available history. A final note can satisfy its output schema and still cite another ticker. Ask students to locate one check at each boundary in agent.py and tools.py. Types help define the interface, while application code must enforce scope and financial meaning.

title: Trace: three requests for a calculation
callout: Run 05_tool_call_lifecycle.py and follow each call ID.
notes: Before running the script, ask students for three counts: function entries, actual calculations, and model requests. The answers are two entries, one calculation, and four requests including the final structured answer. Inspect the tool-return messages to see how validation feedback reaches the next request. The invalid first call never enters Python. The second enters but fails a semantic check. The third succeeds. This makes the distinction between schema validation and business validation concrete.

title: What the counters mean
callout: A successful-call limit does not bound every invalid request.
notes: The pinned SDK defines RunUsage.tool_calls as successful calls. Its tool_calls_limit uses that count. Request limits remain necessary for repeated schema or semantic failures. Our application dispatcher separately reserves each research action before executing it, including failures after dispatch. Planning and memory tools count toward the SDK limit but do not go through that research dispatcher. These are different measurements with different purposes. Source: installed pydantic_ai/usage.py and 05_tool_call_lifecycle.py.

title: Errors the model can repair
notes: Ask what the model should do differently after each result. A request for twelve prices can be corrected to three if the task permits it. An unknown citation can be replaced with a returned evidence ID. A database outage rarely improves when the model rephrases its question. Avoid treating service failure as an empty dataset because the model may interpret absence as a research finding. Feedback should explain the repairable constraint without hiding the underlying error category.

title: A result needs its interpretation
table: Why it travels with the number
notes: Show the actual metrics payload in the evidence table. The sample AAPL volatility is about 30.29% over the fixture window. The estimator is sample standard deviation of daily log returns times the square root of 252. Returns use adjusted close, and holdings valuation uses raw close. A source excerpt needs equivalent context: ticker, period, publication date, units, and locator. Ask what happens if a chunk keeps Debt: 100 but drops the USD millions header. Source: research_harness/data.py and Lecture 4 stock-analysis template.

title: A bounded tool response
body: The model can narrow the query when relevant records do not fit.
notes: This is an illustrative response envelope, not a measured result from the sample. Open pack_evidence in retrieval.py. It measures the serialized envelope as well as the records, includes only whole records, and reports omissions. A record too large for the remaining budget stays in the corpus. Cutting JSON after a fixed number of characters could remove a unit, citation ID, or closing delimiter. Our 12,000-character search budget is separate from the agent context token budget. We will test small budgets in script 06.

title: A timeout after a write
body: The tool saves a note and commits.
The acknowledgement never reaches the caller.
The caller retries and may create a second note.
callout: The caller needs a way to recognize the original operation.
notes: Pause after each line and ask what the caller knows. A timeout establishes that the caller lacks a response. It does not establish that the write failed. Introduce a stable operation key that identifies one business action across retries. Save the full experiment for script 07 in the recovery block. For a local SQLite effect, storing the effect and its receipt in one transaction makes their relationship atomic. For a remote service, local state alone cannot provide that guarantee.

title: Parallel calls and shared state
table: Scope and rate limits remain valid
notes: A response can propose multiple tool calls, but dependencies still matter. Async execution does not remove data races. Our course supervisor runs ticker tasks serially and holds a project lock. Parallelizing it would require atomic task claiming, coordination of provider quotas, and a report-generation policy. Distinguish independent reads from concurrent writes. The memory demonstration later shows an actual version conflict and a deliberate merge.

title: Three identifiers with different jobs
table: One request and its matching response
A calculation with the same effective inputs
callout: A risk cache needs dates, adjustment, input hash, and code version.
notes: A new model attempt can generate a new tool-call ID for the same business action. That makes the call ID insufficient as a stable deduplication key. A cache key answers whether a prior result is reusable, not whether a particular write committed. Ask what is missing from a cache keyed only by AAPL. Include start, cutoff, price adjustment, data hash, and calculation version. An evidence ID identifies the stored observation itself. Reference slide 53 develops this distinction.

title: Break
notes: 9:55–10:05 Pacific. Leave the partial project and retrieval corpus ready for the next block.
subtitle:
10 minutes
Next: memory, retrieval, and context

title: The different jobs of memory
table: Retain a question or provisional conclusion
Coordinate work and restore a conversation
notes: Ask students to classify an exact return, an unresolved refinancing question, a completed plan item, and an attempt count. Explain that these logical responsibilities do not require separate databases, although the capability stores in our application use separate SQLite files. The next request sees only what the context policy loads. A record can be durable but never retrieved. Memory design therefore includes writing, metadata, retrieval, use, update, and retention.

title: The project stores
notes: Run 04_inspect_project.py on a project with AAPL complete and other tickers pending. Locate one item in each store. Ask which records are sufficient to reconstruct the numerical report and which only help the model continue. Task acceptance belongs to the application. A model-written memory entry saying done cannot override a missing or invalid note. Sources: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/memory/, https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/planning/, https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/step-persistence/.

title: What enters memory
table: Hypothesis with an open research question
callout: A later request needs to know what kind of statement it is reading.
notes: The main risk is promoting a provisional statement into an apparent fact through repeated summaries. Ask students how a working note should preserve uncertainty and source attribution. Exact calculations belong in evidence. A summary can point to their IDs and explain what remains unresolved. The current project uses immutable input snapshots. A live research service would need an explicit policy for new source versions, invalidated calculations, and expired observations.

title: The dates in a financial record
callout: A January question cannot use a value first published in February.
notes: Use a balance-sheet value to distinguish economic time from availability time. A historical research cutoff applies to publication, not merely the period end. Ingestion time helps audit our system and can matter when reconstructing what the system knew. Our source fixtures use ISO publication dates in available_on. A larger data model may need timestamps and time zones, especially for intraday decisions. Connect this to timing and leakage discussed in the modeling classes.

title: Corrections and historical questions
body: Keep the relationship between versions and apply it relative to the question date.
notes: These are invented values for the design exercise. Ask what happens if we globally mark the first record superseded and exclude it from every query. The April view loses valid historical evidence. Retain both versions with units, economic period, publication date, source, and a supersedes relationship. A June response should make the correction traceable. Time-to-live is a different policy: a current quote may expire quickly while a dated filing remains useful. Derived values invalidate when their inputs or definition change.

title: Choosing a retrieval method
table: Exact fields, dates, values, and state matter
Both exact terms and semantic matches matter
notes: Avoid treating a vector database as the whole memory system. It still needs write policies, access scope, metadata, and evaluation. Keep original sources and exact numerical fields even when indexing text embeddings. Chunking should preserve table headers and qualifications. Small chunks can lose meaning, while large chunks consume the response budget. Overlap can create near-duplicates. SQLite is sufficient for this small corpus. FTS5 is a possible lexical extension. Source: https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html.

title: Retrieval order changes the answer
table: Rank all, take two, then filter
Future AAPL and MSFT occupy both slots
Eligible AAPL debt and cash excerpts
notes: Query: debt refinancing liquidity. Inspect the five fixture records before execution. The incorrect pipeline spends the top-k budget before checking scope. The correct pipeline limits ticker and publication date first, then ranks the eligible corpus. Three records are eligible and two match this query. The lexical score counts distinct overlapping query terms, with deterministic ties. Ask why adding more global top-k slots only works around this example rather than fixing the ordering policy.

title: Evidence under a response budget
body: Metadata and citation IDs count toward the budget.
Omitted records remain available for another query.
notes: Continue script 06. The exact counts come from this fixture and its evidence envelopes. Open pack_evidence to see that each candidate includes the full response metadata. It can skip a record that does not fit and consider a later smaller one. Ask what retrieval diversity and ranking consequences that policy may have. Character limits are easy to inspect but do not equal token limits. The production search tool in the lesson uses 12,000 characters and a requested limit from one to five.

title: A lexical miss
body: Possible changes include a domain vocabulary, query rewriting, or semantic retrieval.
code:
query = "rollover obligations"

# The source discusses "debt" and "refinancing".
# The lexical baseline returns no match.
callout: The evaluation needs questions beyond the one we just repaired.
notes: Show the debt excerpt and ask whether it is relevant to the query despite zero overlapping terms. An empty result says something about the corpus and retrieval policy, not about the existence of company debt. Discuss stemming versus synonyms: stemming alone does not connect these particular terms. A manual rewrite fixes the known example, while a broader policy needs held-out questions. Script 08 will measure the baseline and the rewrite after the recovery block.

title: Chunks, duplicates, and disagreements
body: Keep a value with its units, period, and table header.
Near-duplicate excerpts can crowd out another source.
Conflicting statements need their provenance and definitions.
notes: Ask students to imagine five retrieved excerpts that repeat the same press release. A larger result count may add little evidence. Deduplication or source diversity can help, but these policies need evaluation against the question. When two sources disagree, inspect whether they describe the same period and measure. Ranking score alone does not settle which statement is correct. Keep original locators and source hashes so a reviewer can return to the document.

title: Allocating a 24,000-token context
notes: These are design numbers, not observed usage from the demo. Split the first row into 2,000 instructions and 2,000 schemas, and the last into 2,000 answer reserve and 2,000 headroom. Ask what to do when a new excerpt needs 6,000 tokens. Students should explain which evidence or history becomes less accessible, rather than simply declaring a larger context. Provider limits and actual tokenization determine capacity. Source result limits and conversation compaction operate at different levels.

title: Trimming, summarizing, and retrieving
table: Keeps recent detail, can lose earlier reasons
Keeps a narrative, can omit or alter facts
Restores exact records, can miss relevant ones
callout: Our SlidingWindowCompaction trims history without writing a summary.
notes: Open the configured capability: max_tokens=24000 and keep_tokens=12000. Explain that the trigger and retention target also interact with other retention rules, including message limits. The capability preserves valid tool-call/result relationships. Exact evidence remains in the application store, but a later model request must retrieve it. Ask what happens if the original research question falls out of history. Keep scope in instructions and dependencies, with current investigation state in a short working note. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/compaction/.

title: A useful working summary
notes: A summary should help the next request choose useful work. Keep exact financial values retrievable rather than relying only on paraphrase. Distinguish an observation from an attributed claim or hypothesis. Source excerpts and model-written notes can contain text that looks like instructions. Treat that material as research input. Application rules such as ticker scope and cutoff remain enforced in Python. Ask how a summary that says leverage improved could lose the definition or period needed to interpret it.

title: Concurrent memory edits
table: A and B read a note
callout: The second half of script 06 uses SqliteMemoryStore.
notes: This is an actual capability-store experiment, not a simulated concurrency API. The script reads the same note twice, writes A with its expected version, and catches MemoryConflictError on B. It then rereads and deliberately merges. Ask whether simply concatenating two contradictory conclusions would resolve the research disagreement. Optimistic concurrency prevents a silent lost update. Semantic resolution still requires evidence and judgment. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/memory/.

title: Scope and retention
body: Project and ticker scope come from application dependencies.
A shared service also needs authenticated user or organization scope.
Report citations need retrievable evidence after scratch notes expire.
notes: Use the project directory and ticker namespace to explain the present boundary. A model should not select arbitrary namespaces in a shared service. Retention policies differ by record role: scratch notes, transcripts, caches, and accepted evidence have different uses. Removing a cached calculation is recoverable if inputs and code remain. Removing the only copy of cited source evidence can break an existing report. Ask which records students would retain to reconstruct an investigation six months later.

title: Break
notes: 10:55–11:05 Pacific. Prepare fresh paths for the recovery demonstration. The source and code hashes must match the current implementation.
subtitle:
10 minutes
Next: recovery and longer research projects

title: What a checkpoint restores
notes: A checkpoint captures a point in the conversation, not the entire world. On restart, previous_history searches prior attempts for a settled snapshot and provides its messages to a new agent run. The new run ID identifies the new attempt. The conversation identity remains the ticker. Explain why capability state and application state still require their own storage and compatibility policies. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/step-persistence/.

title: Recovery after a settled calculation
body: The second worker restores the calculation result.
The price calculation runs once across two attempts.
code:
uv run python 03_resume_research.py runs/class-recovery
uv run python 04_inspect_project.py runs/class-recovery
notes: Run the demonstration and inspect the resumed_from event. It deliberately interrupts after a calculation has a settled result. Ask students to locate the evidence record and step snapshot. Then change the hypothetical interruption point: what if evidence committed but the tool result did not settle? The call may repeat. A content-derived evidence ID keeps the identical observation from becoming a duplicate record, but the calculation itself could run again. The distinction is between reusing settled conversation state and deduplicating effects.

title: The interruption point matters
notes: Walk through the state changes rather than treating resume as a single feature. The supervisor persists attempt counts before starting work. It validates saved notes before accepting completion. A worker can stop between commits to separate stores. Ask what evidence is available at each boundary and which operation might repeat. Remote writes need an additional row: uncertain acknowledgement requires reconciliation or remote idempotency support. The next slide runs that local lost-acknowledgement case.

title: Recovery after a lost acknowledgement
table: Stable key with effect and receipt
notes: The second implementation stores the effect and its receipt atomically in SQLite. The retry uses project-17:AAPL:debt-question:v1 and the same arguments, so it returns the existing note ID. Reusing the key with different arguments raises an error. Ask students to change the key on every retry and predict the result. A local receipt cannot make a remote service write atomic with a local transaction. A durable workflow engine automates scheduling and replay but does not remove this boundary.

title: Budgets at different levels
notes: Planning and memory tools count toward the successful-call limit. The application separately reserves dispatched research actions before executing them. run --seconds limits a supervisor invocation, while persisted attempt counts prevent unlimited fresh starts. Ask which budget stops repeated schema failures, a hanging function, and repeated successful plan rewrites. The process deadline can stop local work, but it cannot roll back an external effect. A forced stop may also prevent the final usage receipt from being written.

title: Retry ownership
table: Respect retry timing and total deadline
callout: 2 task attempts × 3 SDK attempts × 3 HTTP attempts = 18
notes: The multiplication is an illustrative upper bound for nested retries. Ask which layer should own each category and how total attempts appear in logs. Repeated retries do not fix a deterministic data error. Backoff and jitter help transient service failures but must fit the overall deadline. Avoid resetting cumulative task budgets every time the terminal command starts. Keep usage and events observable so the cost of recovery can be evaluated.

title: Plans and measurable progress
body: The model plan organizes work within a ticker.
The application queue owns attempts and acceptance.
New evidence and resolved questions show research progress.
Repeated plan edits may consume the budget without advancing the answer.
notes: Use a refinancing plan with a debt schedule, cash comparison, disclosure review, and cited conclusion. Ask students to define a completion condition for each step. Research AAPL is vague, while produce a dated risk calculation and source-supported interpretation is testable. More agents would add ownership and conflict-resolution questions. Evaluate whether planning helps through repeated provider-backed runs with the same budgets. The fixed demo sequence cannot measure the quality benefit of planning.

title: Compatibility when a project resumes
body: The configuration records inputs, dates, model, and budgets.
Hashes identify the data, source corpus, code, and dependency lock.
Changed inputs or tool meanings require a new project or an explicit migration.
notes: Open config.json and code_fingerprint. The current application uses the straightforward new-project policy. Replaying messages that describe one calculation against a changed implementation can create inconsistency even when the tool name and Python imports still work. A production service can add migrations, but must define which historical messages and state remain compatible. Saved input paths are absolute, so moving the project to a new computer also calls for recreating the setup.

title: The saved project in use
code:
uv run python research.py init runs/class-project
uv run python research.py run runs/class-project --max-tasks 1
uv run python 04_inspect_project.py runs/class-project
uv run python research.py run runs/class-project
notes: The first run exits 2 because the report is incomplete. Inspect AAPL with attempts=1 and two pending tickers. The next invocation completes the remaining work and keeps AAPL at one attempt. Running the completed project again starts no new work. Use the store contents to revisit the difference between evidence, memory, plan, and task state. If time is tight, inspect the preflight project instead of waiting for another full run.

title: Accepting a research note
table: Records exist for the assigned ticker
Metrics and a dated source are present
notes: Open ResearchNote and validate_note. The application checks citation existence, scope, and required evidence kinds both during output validation and before saving. These checks do not establish the semantic support for every sentence. A note can cite a real volatility record and still make an unsupported earnings forecast. A claim-level output schema could make this review easier by connecting individual claims to records. Source: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/output/.

title: The report preserves coverage
body: Numerical tables come from saved calculations.
Accepted notes cite retrievable evidence.
Failed tickers and actual observation windows remain visible.
Portfolio weights require every holding in the denominator.
notes: Open examples/report.html and follow one evidence ID into evidence.json. Ask what would happen if a missing holding disappeared from portfolio value. The weights of the remaining holdings would change meaning. The report withholds portfolio weights when the required holding results are incomplete. It also shows requested and actual dates. For strict comparisons, a future module could require a common window across tickers rather than only exposing the difference.

title: Evaluation at the failure boundary
table: Relevant records, correct scope, stale edits
No duplicate intended write after retry
notes: A plausible final report can conceal a retrieval failure. Tests should target the mechanism that can fail. The lecture suite exercises numerical conventions, input snapshots, citation repair, actual capability stores, task and request budgets, checkpoint recovery, retrieval ordering, output budgets, and idempotent writes. Provider-backed quality evaluation additionally needs repeated runs and review of claim support. Keep traces so a disappointing report can be connected to the retrieval or decision that caused it.

title: A small retrieval evaluation
notes: Recall is relevant expected records retrieved divided by all expected relevant records. The script also reports precision among returned records, defined as zero when no result returns. Each of these four questions has one expected supporting record. The rewrite fixes rollover obligations by searching debt refinancing. Explain that tuning and testing on the same query establishes a repaired example, not general retrieval quality. Add held-out questions, duplicates, conflicts, and hard scope/date failures before selecting a policy.

title: Designing a leverage module
notes: Ask students to design the module before naming libraries. The ratio definition determines the data requirements. A negative denominator may produce a numerical ratio that needs different interpretation. Decide whether the output is available, undefined, or accompanied by a structured reason. Then add model arguments, dependencies, retry and cache policies, acceptance checks, and a report section. A Papermill tool can fit this architecture if it accepts validated parameters, runs in an isolated directory with a deadline, and returns structured results.

title: Paired design exercise
body: Option A: retain a February debt figure and its May correction. Explain April and June retrieval.
Option C: change the write key on every retry. Predict the effect, then restore a stable key.
callout: Five minutes: show the records or the sequence of writes.
notes: Pairs choose one concrete exercise from lesson.md. For A, require units, economic period, publication date, source, and the relationship between versions. For C, require a stable intended-operation identity and consistent arguments. Avoid accepting a general statement such as use a database. Students should show enough detail that another pair can follow the query or retry. Use the next slide for a short discussion.

title: Discussion of the designs
table: Historical questions need their original view
Retries identify the same intended effect
A key must refer to a consistent operation
notes: Use three minutes for two pairs to explain their answers. Ask one counterfactual for each: what if every superseded record disappears globally, or what if a new call ID becomes the operation key? The first breaks historical reconstruction. The second allows the same effect to repeat across attempts. These are examples of how a small interface or storage decision changes the correctness of the whole research workflow.

title: The complete research application
body: Open report.html, summary.json, and evidence.json in the project directory.
code:
uv run python research.py init runs/final
uv run python research.py run runs/final
uv run python 04_inspect_project.py runs/final
notes: Use the final two minutes to locate the deliverables and continuation exercises. The application works with the sample CSV or the Lecture 4 database. The demo uses predictable responses through the actual Pydantic agent runtime. A configured provider chooses its own tool sequence. Students should now be able to explain why the application keeps different kinds of state, validates tool boundaries, and treats a checkpoint separately from an effect receipt. Exercises B, D, E, F, and G extend the work after class.

title: Reference: the capability configuration
code:
Planning(store=plan_store, tools=["write_plan"])
Memory(memory_store, namespace=ticker, max_tokens=1200)
SlidingWindowCompaction(
    max_tokens=24000, keep_tokens=12000,
)
StepPersistence(store=step_store, run_id=attempt_id)
notes: Reference slide, outside the 180-minute live route. Open agent.py for complete constructor names and SQLite paths. The working-memory injection budget and conversation compaction threshold solve different problems. The plan session and memory namespace use the assigned ticker within the project directory. Step persistence uses a unique attempt ID so a new run can refer back to settled history. Sources: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/ and linked capability pages.

title: Reference: cache identity
body: A benchmark result also needs the benchmark identity and its source hash.
code:
cache_key = hash((
    ticker, start, as_of,
    price_adjustment,
    source_sha256,
    calculation_version,
))
notes: This pseudocode illustrates the logical inputs rather than a portable implementation of hashing. Use deterministic serialization and a stable hash for a persistent cache. Python built-in hash is not a cross-process persistence format. The current evidence store uses canonical JSON and SHA-256. A cache key identifies reusable computation inputs, while a content-derived evidence ID identifies an observation. Ask how changing the return convention should affect each.

title: Reference: a dated memory record
body: Store exact fields where they can be filtered and checked.
code:
entity, kind, value, unit
period_end, available_at, ingested_at
source_hash, document_locator
calculation_version
status, supersedes
notes: This is a suggested schema for a richer statement-data module, not a claim that every field is already implemented. Explain each time field with the December 31, February 2, February 3 example. Record relationships allow corrections without deleting historical evidence. Model-written hypotheses need a kind or status that preserves uncertainty. A vector index can refer back to these records, but should not become the only copy of numerical facts or source provenance.

title: Reference: repeated context cost
code:
input_tokens ≈ n*C + R*n*(n-1)/2

C = 4000; n = 8
R = 1500  # 74,000 total input tokens
R =  500  # 46,000 total input tokens
notes: Derive the sum: the first request has fixed context C, the next C+R, then C+2R, through C+(n-1)R. This ignores compaction and provider caching and excludes output tokens. It illustrates why growing history can make long investigations expensive. Cached input may receive different billing, but retaining irrelevant context still affects attention and capacity. These are token arithmetic examples, not current provider prices. The lesson contains the full explanation.

title: Reference: a retrieval evaluation set
notes: Keep development queries separate from held-out evaluation queries. Add expected source IDs and a reason each source supports the question. Measure recall and precision alongside scope/date violations, serialized size, latency, and final claim support. A result can pass lexical relevance and still be unavailable at the research date. If a model rewrites queries, retain the original question, rewritten query, and retrieved IDs so the evaluator can locate the source of a failure.

title: Reference: continuation exercises
notes: See lesson.md for the full prompts and teaching_guide.md for discussion points. Exercise E has stock return 2%, benchmark return 1%, and a difference of 1 percentage point. It also needs compatible calendars and endpoint definitions. Exercise F asks why a real historical volatility citation cannot establish next-quarter earnings growth. Exercise G requires repeated provider-backed runs under the same conditions. A deterministic model remains useful for runtime tests but cannot demonstrate better research decisions.
